GO:0055085 is defined as transport of a solute across a lipid bilayer. The essence (LptB powers a transport process) is right, so the better term is the specific process GO:0015920 lipopolysaccharide transport, which LptB already carries experimentally (not an is_a descendant; a lateral correction). The P. putida LptB review makes the same MODIFY for the same mechanistic reason, because the E. coli evidence argues the transmembrane framing is inaccurate.

LptG does part of the work of building the LPS outer leaflet; it forms half of the cavity that extracts LPS for delivery to the outer membrane, and LptG depletion leaves an abnormal envelope and a defective permeability barrier. The term is accepted as core, together with lipopolysaccharide transport (GO:0015920), consistently across all seven E. coli Lpt reviews.

GO:0055085 is defined as transport of a solute across a lipid bilayer from one side to the other. LptB2FG does not translocate LPS across the inner membrane (MsbA does); it extracts LPS out of the periplasmic leaflet into the periplasmic bridge. The generic term is therefore both uninformative and mechanistically imprecise; the supported specific process is lipopolysaccharide transport, which the gene already carries.

Correct but generic. GO:0062051 lipopolysaccharide transport system (is_a transporter complex) is the specific term for the transenvelope Lpt machine, and its definition is based on this very paper. LptG is part of that system as a subunit of the inner-membrane LptB2FGC module.

GO:0140332 (removes LPS from the outer leaflet of a donor membrane, moves it through the aqueous phase in a hydrophobic pocket and delivers it to the outer leaflet of an acceptor membrane) is the activity of the Lpt bridge as a whole. LptG performs part of it, extraction from the donor membrane, as one half of the LPS-binding cavity, so the contributes_to qualifier is used. GO:0015221 lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transporter activity is not used, because E. coli structures show LptB2FG extrudes LPS out of the membrane rather than across it. The comparator LptC carries GO:0140332, and the P. putida LptG review uses the same contributes_to GO:0140332 core term.
